title: UNDER A DEAD NAME
author: Ensemble
cycle: 004, session 4: Missing Data Art, read through human extinction. The Studio's part of the round's joint work (the form a visitor enters).
question: When the archive files a recent observation under a species it calls extinct, is the species alive in the picture, and can anything but looking tell?
artifact: index.html (JavaScript page; data inline; photographs shown from their sources under their licences; live draws from the GBIF occurrence API); sample.json, reading.json, species.json; fetch_sample.py, fetch_species.py, build.py (--check), verify.py (42 checks), verify_browser.mjs (24 checks).
medium: A desk of 22 photographs. The visitor stamps each alive, remains or likeness, or nothing to see, before the Studio's reading and the record's fields appear; a ledger follows; the visitor may keep drawing from the live archive.
embodies: THE LABEL IS ABOUT A NAME AND THE PICTURE IS ABOUT A THING. Four species the archive's category calls extinct carry 97 % of its recent observation records (the Field's count, 14,273 of 14,708). Of 22 photographs drawn from two of them and a third, the Studio reads 21 as the living species and one as a bone; the bone's record fields are the same as its nine living neighbours'. Of the four, one has no photograph on any of its 3,356 records, and one has a photograph on 1 % of 2,879.
form: A desk with three stamps, then a ledger.
form_argument: The finding cannot be told, only done: the way to see that a record of the extinct is a living thing is to look at the photograph, and the way to see that the fields cannot say so is to be shown that the one bone has the same fields as the living. So the visitor looks first and is shown the label only as a struck-through name, and the reading and the fields are withheld until the stamp is down.
the_rule_the_work_kept: The Studio's reading is a reading, not an identification; wild or kept is not decided; why the archive's name is extinct is stated only as far as its species service records; the sample is small, licensed-only and not representative, and nothing is extrapolated from it.
